newsitem.title: GERMANY: German call money rates ease to 3.00/3.05 pct.
newsitem.headline: German call money rates ease to 3.00/3.05 pct.

text.p: German call money rates were slightly lower on Thursday at about 3.00/3.05 percent compared with 3.05 percent on Wednesday, traders said.
The lower rates came after the Bundesbank injected a net 2.1 billion marks into the market on Wednesday in its weekly tender, traders said.
But traders said demand would likely remain strong and that rates would not slip below the three percent level, where the Bundesbank has kept the repo rate fixed for some weeks.
The Bundesbank, as expected, kept interest rates steady at its council meeting on Thursday and the repo at three percent.
"The Bundesbank gave the market what it needed," said one Frankfurt trader about the alloction.
Another reason for the lower rates was an increase in commercial bank reserves at the Bundesbank.
The bank said deposits as of Wednesday stood at 39.8 billion marks, up from 37.6 billion marks, while the monthly average rose to 37.5 billion marks from 37.2 billion marks.
Lombard borrowings were pegged at about 100 million marks.
The Frankfurt Interbank Overnight Average FIONA= was down at 3.06167 percent compared with 3,07650 on Wednesday.
